newsitem.title: CHINA: China bank experts see convertible yuan as stable.
newsitem.headline: China bank experts see convertible yuan as stable.

text.p: The Chinese yuan is expected to remain stable after becoming convertible under the current account on December 1, the official Xinhua news agency on Friday quoted experts as saying.

Yuan convertibility was a reflection and result of the smooth operation of China's new foreign currency exchange system since January 1994, Xinhua quoted Tao Liming of the Bank of China's International Finance Research Institute as saying.
The move was not expected to have any great impact on the domestic foreign exchange market, Tao said.
"The chances of wild fluctuations in the local currency's exchange rate are very remote," Xinhua quoted him as saying.

Analysts believed the remaining restrictions on transactions under the capital account, which includes direct investment, international loans and securities trading, would help ensure the yuan's stability, it said without elaborating.
